critique: The delivered contribution is exact population identification on the certified double-triangular class: it proves rectangular certificate sufficiency, same-class quotient identification, intrinsic dimension, and termination and completeness of an exhaustive exact-real algorithm. It does not prove that the local certificate is necessary for heterogeneous alphabets, but the prose consistently limits the claimed equivalence to equal-q selected alphabets and supplies a counterexample, so there is no stale sharp-frontier claim. The cdmTools consumer remains only a population specification: the algorithm relies on exact equality, rank, and conditional-independence queries, while multiplicity-calibrated finite-sample inference is left open. This absence of a usable statistical procedure or computational implementation limits the leading-journal score despite the field-level identification theorem. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
